thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stocks Edge Higher After Softer-than-expected Jobs Report

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stocks Edge Higher After Softer-than-expected Jobs Report
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch
U.S. economy added 157,000 jobs in July, compared with 195,000 forecast
U.S. stock-market indexes rose tentatively higher on Friday, after the July jobs report came in below expectations, although a drop in the unemployment rate and increases to the previous two months indicate the labor market remains healthy.
Investors also grappled with fresh news that China would retaliate with tariffs on $60 billion in U.S. goods, at a time when trade deficit rose for the first time in four months.
What are benchmarks doing?
The S&P 500 rose 3 points, or 0.1%, to 2,829, with nine of its 11 sectors trading higher.
The Nasdaq Composite Index fell 9 points, or less than 0.1%, to 7,793, taking a breather after a 1.1% rally fueled by Apple Inc.'s share advance on Thursday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 36 points, or 0.1% to 25,363.
What's driving markets?
Wall Street has been caught up in a battle between concerns over the U.S.'s trade spats with China and optimism over economic and quarterly earnings results that have been outstanding by most measures.
Market reaction to Friday's nonfarm-payrolls report for July was largely muted. The yearly rate of wage gains was unchanged at 2.7%, suggesting no immediate pressure on inflation.
The Federal Reserve's latest policy update affirmed the central bank's plan to raise interest rates at least once more this year, and the jobs report wasn't seen as likely to change that narrative.
Check out:U.S. jobs report for July likely to be another good one, but the real story is rising wages (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-jobs-report-for-july-likely-to-be-another-good-one-but-the-real-story-is-rising-wages-2018-08-02)
What are analysts are saying?
"The latest jobs reports means that the economy is chugging along, we are still adding jobs this late in the cycle while we had double-digit revenue and earnings growth," said Michael Antonelli, equity sales trader at Robert W. Baird & Co.
"It looks as though the risk to trade wars is asymmetric to upside. All the bad news is priced in, but if we get some kind of resolution with China, then markets will rip higher," Antonelli said.
What else is on investors' radar?
The trade deficit rose 7% in June (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-trade-deficit-climbs-7-still-on-track-to-hit-10-year-high-2018-08-03)to mark the first increase in four months, keeping the U.S. on track to post the largest annual gap in a decade even as the Trump White House escalates tariffs in an effort to bring it down.
Beyond the jobs report and trade data, investors will await the ISM nonmanufacturing index for July due to be released at 10 a.m.
Elsewhere, investors are watching signs of economic slowdown in China. A private gauge showed service sector activity in the country continued to grow in July, but at a slower pace than in June (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chinas-caixin-pmi-shows-services-activity-cooling-2018-08-03). China's economy, already facing a slide, has been hurt by the tariff clash with the U.S.
Key Chinese equity index the Shanghai Composite fell 1%, while the Shenzhen Composite declined by 1.7% after hitting a 3 1/2 -year closing low in the prior session.
Which stocks are in focus?
Dish Network Corp. (DISH)soared (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dish-networks-stock-soars-as-earnings-and-revenue-beat-expectations-2018-08-03) 9%, after the satellite pay-TV service reported better-than-expected second-quarter earnings and revenue.
Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) climbed 6.7% after reporting second-quarter earnings.
Shares of CBS Corp. (CBSA) will be in focus after the media company late-Thursday reported second-quarter earnings that came in below expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-shares-down-slightly-after-media-company-misses-expectations-2018-08-02) but narrowly topped revenue forecasts for the quarter. CBS on Wednesday said its board of directors had hired outside lawyers to conduct an investigation into allegations that Chief Executive Les Moonves had sexually harassed women. Thursday's earnings statement made no mention (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-earnings-call-oddly-silent-on-allegations-against-moonves-2018-08-02) of Moonves' status.
Apple(AAPL) made history on Thursday become the first U.S. company on Thursday to reach a valuation of $1 trillion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-1-trillion-heres-the-meltdown-that-followed-the-first-company-to-get-there-2018-08-01), following its better-than-expected quarterly results.
Shares of Groupon Inc.(GRPN) are down sharply after the company posted weaker-than-expected second-quarter results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/groupon-stock-falls-after-earnings-revenue-miss-expectations-2018-08-03).
